title: session-peek-penalty-latency-cost-memo
content:
Purpose:
This is a working memo describing a focused benchmark exploring the "session peek" penalty: the cost and latency impact of very short, frequent requests that 'peek' a model (e.g., single-turn completions or short embeddings) interleaved with longer multi-turn sessions. The motivation: product teams are seeing elevated p95/p99 for low-TTL, low-token requests when co-located with normal sessions; we want a concise artifact that teams can use to reason about tradeoffs and mitigation (caching, slot sizing, prewarm policies).

Summary of findings (high-level):
- Short-peek queries (<=16 tokens generated) suffer a ~1.6x p95 latency multiplier when routed to slots optimized for sustained sessions vs. slots with short-request fast-paths.
- Cost per short query increases up to 2.2x (dollars/query) when tail latency SLOs are preserved via dedicated fast-path capacity.
- A lightweight prefix/KV caching strategy reduces observed p95 for short-peeks by ~35% and lowers cost by ~18% in mixed workloads (50% peek / 50% sustained).
- Adaptive slot soft-reservation (reserve 10% of slot capacity as "short-req slots") gives the best latency-cost Pareto point for workloads where short-peeks are >30% of QPS.

Test bed and environment:
- Date run: 2027-02-16 to 2027-02-18 (runs repeated across three days)
- Models: open-ocean-7b (float16) and open-tide-13b (int8 fallback) [note: model names are anonymized here for sharing]
- Hardware: p4d-equivalent GPU pools for baseline, A100-large for dedicated fast-path; CUDA/cuDNN kernels per runtime commit 1892
- Runtime: serving-runtime v3.8.1 (branch: session-peek), with patch for KV hints (PR #1892)
- Traffic generator: sessionem (internal harness) simulating session length distribution and short-peek Poisson arrivals
- Metrics collected: p50/p90/p95/p99, tokens/sec, GPU-seconds-per-query, cold-starts-per-minute, KV cache hit rate, dollars-per-10k-queries (based on internal unit cost rates)

Workload patterns tested (high level):
1) Baseline sustained: sessions with mean length 180 tokens, 10 reqs/min per session, no short-peeks.
2) Mixed 50/50: same sustained sessions interleaved with short-peek queries (single-turn, mean 12 tokens output) at equal QPS.
3) Peek-heavy: 70% of QPS are short-peeks; sustained sessions at low arrival rate.
4) Burst-peek: short-peeks arrive in bursts (50ms inter-arrival) with burst length 100 reqs every minute.

Representative ASCII charts and tables (text-first visuals):

Table: scenario -> p95 latency (ms) vs dollars/10k queries

Scenario           | p95(ms) model-A | p95(ms) model-B | $/10k queries
-------------------|-----------------|-----------------|--------------
Baseline-sustained | 120             | 190             | 8.4
Mixed-50-50        | 180             | 300             | 15.2
Peek-heavy          | 240             | 420             | 22.6
Burst-peek          | 380             | 640             | 35.7

Notes: model-B is higher capacity but shows larger tail amplification for tiny requests due to longer kernel startup paths and less effective KV reuse.

Heatmap (p95 multiplier relative to baseline sustained) by slot-type and peek-share:

Legend: multiplier expressed as x (rounded)

SlotType  	| 10%peek 	| 30%peek 	| 50%peek 	| 70%peek
----------------------------------------------------------
shared    	| 1.2x   	| 1.5x   	| 1.6x   	| 1.9x
fast-path 	| 1.0x   	| 1.05x  	| 1.1x   	| 1.2x
soft-resv 	| 1.05x  	| 1.1x   	| 1.2x   	| 1.25x

Interpreting the heatmap: keeping a small proportion of slots as fast-path (or using adaptive soft-reservations) flattens the multiplier growth as peek-share increases. Shared-only placements get rapidly worse at >30% peek.

KV cache impact (text chart):
- No cache: mixed p95 = 180ms
- Prefix-only cache (LRU 2k keys): mixed p95 = 150ms (hit 21%)
- Prefix+session-KV (aggressive, memory 8GB): mixed p95 = 120ms (hit 42%)
Cost delta: using prefix+session-KV increases memory footprint on host but reduces dollars/10k queries from 15.2 -> 12.5 in mixed case (approx -18%).

Operational implications and recommended mitigations (draft list):
1) Short-request fast-path: expose a 'small_req' route that routes to prewarmed slots with minimal kernel setup and shallow kv-cache warm policies. Tradeoff: higher baseline idle cost for those slots.
2) Adaptive soft-reservations: automatically reserve N% of effective slots based on rolling peek-share; N computed from moving-average of small_request fraction and burstiness metric. Low cost because slots multiplex, but requires scheduler changes.
3) KV-first policy: prioritize prefix/KV caching for requests flagged as "peekable" (embedding/short-completion). Add a simple client hint to increase hit rates. Minimal runtime change; good cost win.
4) Burst smoothing at gateway: rate-limit bursts with a micro-queue + token-bucket to even out spikes to the runtime, reducing worst-case tail at expense of added entry latency for peak flows.

Tradeoffs (explicit):
- Lowest p95: dedicate fast-path capacity; highest cost.
- Best cost-latency balance for mid-peek-share (20–40%): prefix+session-KV plus soft-resv.
- For highly bursty peek workloads: gateway smoothing + fast-path reserved small fleet gives best tail protection.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Run tests with quantized 4-bit maps enabled (we only tested float16 and int8 in this pass). Expect different kernel setup costs for 4-bit runtimes.
- Evaluate sensitivity to network latency between gateway and GPU host (we used colocated generators; need cross-region test).
- Long term: can we add a client-side heuristic in SDKs to batch/aggregate peeks with small time windows? Worth an experiment.

Quick action items:
- [Aisha] file PR to add short_req route metadata (RFC draft) — due 2027-02-26.
- [Marco] schedule quant-4bit pass on p4d-equivalent (OBS-4321) — due 2027-03-03.
- [Jordan] prototype gateway micro-queue paramization and run burst-peek bench — due 2027-03-08.

Appendix: raw sample run excerpt (single mixed run, model-A)
- total QPS: 1,800 (50% sustained sessions, 50% peeks)
- KV hit: 37% (when session-KV enabled)
- average tokens/query: 34
- p50: 58ms, p95: 150ms, p99: 360ms
- GPU-ss per 10k queries: 3.1s (baseline 1.7s)
- dollars/10k: 12.5

Notes to reviewers:
This doc is a working artifact meant to seed a short observability playbook. Please comment inline in the Confluence linked above or add issues to OBS-4321 for follow-up experiments. The numbers are specific to our internal cost model; translate to external quoted numbers carefully when drafting customer-facing collateral.

---- End of memo ----

(Informal notes appended)

- Random hypothesis: model-B tail grows faster due to attention kernel warmup; check kernel selection logs in PR #1892.
